narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Siva Tau was composed during the 1980s to replace the traditional Maulu'ulu Moa.
It was first performed in 1991 for the Rugby World Cup, intended to provide a more effective psychological boost for the players.
on_screen: Map: Samoa · Oceania
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: It is performed before matches to express Samoan identity, pride, and dominance.
It serves as a challenge to opponents and a psychological tool for the performers.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: File:Siva Tau.webm (https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/bf/Siva_Tau.webm?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance involves military-style gestures.
Performers mimic the handling of a spear, strike their knees, and challenge their opponents through direct, aggressive movements.
The performance is accompanied by a vocal chant.
Watch for Spear Handling, Knee Strike.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (kUuaJ9fFDX0)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Group formation facing the opposition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music consists of a vocal chant performed by the athletes.
The lyrics are in the Samoan language.
Listen for the Vocal chant.
The sound is defined by a collective, rhythmic vocal chant that is both musical and menacing, emphasizing the power of the Samoan language.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The Usos (WWE performers) are noted for using the Siva Tau in their ring entrances.
The Toa Samoa rugby league team uses a variant where 'Toa' replaces 'Manu' in the lyrics.
The Siva Tau is a descendant of traditional Polynesian war dances, replacing the Maulu'ulu Moa in the context of Samoan national sports.

scenes.title: Step A — slowly
narration: Step 1: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart in a firm, grounded stance.
Step 2: Mimic the motion of holding and thrusting a spear with the arms.
Drill: Practice the grounded stance.
on_screen: Instructor front view, then back view (student's perspective); three repetitions

scenes.title: Step B — the next layer
narration: Step 3: Perform rhythmic strikes to the knees or thighs to emphasize the beat.
Step 4: Maintain a steady, aggressive vocal chant in unison with the group.
Drill: Repeat the chant lyrics in rhythm.
on_screen: Instructor front and back view; slow, then half tempo

scenes.title: Put it together
narration: Step A, then Step B, without stopping. Slow first.
Now half tempo. Now full tempo.
Mirror: the instructor faces you and mirrors, so your right is your right.
Drill: Coordinate the knee strikes with the chant.
